title: LHS work convergence and grid-independence of ΔF are assumed, not established

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: major.**

Theorem 1 *assumes* (i) $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle := \lim_{\Delta t\to0}\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle_\Pi$ exists and (ii) $\Delta F$ is grid-independent. Part (b) of the problem asks to *establish* a well-defined bound in the continuous-actuation limit, which includes controlling the physical (left-hand) side. The proof merely passes a limit through an inequality whose LHS limit is hypothesized.

**Consequence:** the theorem is conditional on an unverified physical hypothesis about the protocol; nothing rules out $\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle_\Pi$ failing to converge.

**Suggested fix (clean):** restate the conclusion as a $\limsup$ bound,
$$\limsup_{\Delta t\to0}\langle W_{\mathrm{ext}}\rangle_\Pi \le -\Delta F + k_B T\,\mathcal I_{[0,\tau]},$$
which follows from the per-grid inequality plus monotone convergence of the information term **without** assuming LHS convergence. This removes the unverifiable hypothesis. If LHS convergence is genuinely wanted, it must be proved for the model class (e.g. via convergence of the controlled diffusion's work functional).
